subject: Context slabization and proration example for pilot pricing
messages:

Subject: Re: Pilot scope and a couple of billing questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo — the latency numbers looked great. Before procurement signs off we need to understand how you would bill our main use case: a long product catalog context (roughly 150k tokens ingested per day) with many short runtime queries against cached prefixes. Specifically: how does Redwood "slice" that big context for metering, how are per-request minimums applied, and what rounding rules would apply to 1) the ingest/embedding step and 2) the runtime chat calls that hit the cached KV?

Procurement also asked if you can provide a simple worked example so they can reconcile to our internal forecasting. Can you send a sample calculation and any suggested concessions for a pilot (30 days, up to 200k tokens/day)?

Appreciate it — Tom

FlexRetail

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@flexretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and a couple of billing questions

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Putting a short worked example below and attaching a matrix; letting Grace and Sergio flag anything we should change before we send to ProcureOps.

High-level summary (short):
- We bill generation/serving tokens and ingestion tokens separately.
- Billing quantum: charges are rounded up to the nearest 64-token quantum for per-call accounting (this is to keep metering stable for micro-calls).
- Minimum per runtime call: 256-token floor applies when the request hits a fresh model execution (waived if served entirely from cached KV prefix).
- Context "slabization": for long context stores we chunk the context into 8k-token slabs for storage/lookup; ingest cost is charged pro-rata based on total tokens ingested (no per-slab minimum).

Worked example (pilot daily peak scenario):
Inputs:
- Daily catalog ingest: 150,000 tokens/day (one big batch upload)
- Average runtime call: 420 model tokens generated; 80 tokens of prompt that hit KV-cache prefix (prefix size 2k tokens cached per item)
- Expected runtime calls/day: 1,200

1) Ingest (one-time per-day): 150,000 tokens billed at ingest rate. No minimums per slab. Rounding: we bill exact token counts for ingest (no 64-token quantum).
  - Ingest billed tokens = 150,000

2) Runtime calls (1,200 calls): each call has 80 tokens of prompt (cache-hit) + 420 generated tokens. Metering rules:
  - For cache-hit prompt only: if the request is served from KV without a fresh forward, we do NOT charge the 256-call minimum and only bill the generated tokens (rounded to 64-token quantum).
  - For calls that require a fresh forward (e.g., cache miss or prefix too long), the 256-token minimum applies to the model execution accounting (total prompt+generation), then rounding to 64-token quantum.

Assume conservative mix: 75% cache-hit (no fresh forward), 25% fresh forward.
- Calls with cache-hit (900 calls): bill generated tokens only. Generated 420 tokens rounded up to nearest 64 => 448 tokens billed per call.
  - 900 * 448 = 403,200 billed tokens
- Calls with fresh forward (300 calls): total tokens = 80 + 420 = 500 => minimum floor 256 applies but 500 > 256 so floor not binding; apply 64-token rounding => round 500 up to 512 per call.
  - 300 * 512 = 153,600 billed tokens

Runtime billed tokens/day = 403,200 + 153,600 = 556,800
Total billed tokens/day = ingest (150,000) + runtime (556,800) = 706,800 tokens

Rounding notes: ingest is exact; runtime uses 64-token quantum. Minimum per-request only applies when a fresh forward occurs and total < 256. In this scenario most fresh forwards exceed minimum so minimum is non-binding.

Pilot concession suggestions (what to offer procurement):
- Waive the 256-token per-call minimum for the first 30 days to reduce friction for micro-calls during onboarding.
- 20% off token list price for committed pilot volume up to 200k tokens/day (applies to combined ingest+runtime billed tokens).
- Provide a one-time ingress credit (equal to one day's ingest at list price) to speed PoC approval.

I attached a spreadsheet that models the above with toggles for cache-hit ratio and quantum size. Grace/Sergio: please review and let me know if we should tighten language on quantum vs ingest rounding before I send the formal note to ProcureOps.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Quick notes — looked through the calc. A couple of small edits I recommend before sending to ProcureOps:
- Call out explicitly that policy is: ingest rounding = exact, serving rounding = quantum (64 tokens). That avoids confusion vs older pilots where we rounded ingest.
- Add one worked-row for an extreme case: very small generation (e.g., 20 tokens generated, 40 token prompt) to show how the minimum kicks in (20+40 = 60 => min 256 billed => we can waive for pilot).
- Include a line item for "KV-prefix storage" (we don't charge for persistent storage in the pilot, but for production it's a small per-MB/mo fee) — procurement asks about any hidden line items.

I updated the spreadsheet and added the tiny-call scenario. If we agree on waiver language, I'll draft the short clause for the SOW that says: "For a 30-day pilot Redwood will waive per-call minimums for serving tokens; post-pilot standard minimums apply."

—Grace
Product Lead, Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot scope and a couple of billing questions

Tom / ProcureOps — following internal review we've formalized the example and the pilot concessions. Summary for SOW: 
- Billing rules: ingest charged on exact token counts; serving calls rounded up to 64-token quantum; 256-token per-call minimum applies only to fresh model executions (not to KV-only cache hits).
- Pilot concessions (30 days): 1) waive per-call minimums for all serving calls during the 30-day pilot; 2) 20% discount on billed tokens up to 200k tokens/day; 3) one-time ingest credit equal to one day's average ingest at list price.
- Hidden items: KV-prefix storage is not charged during pilot; post-pilot storage will be billed per-MB at published rates (we've included a sample estimate in the attachment).

Attached: updated FLX_pilot_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (worked examples + toggles). If ProcureOps is good with the SOW language above I can circulate a short SOW and an updated quote.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Monday and we'll lock in pilot start date.

Thanks — Rishi
